title: Update: Card Hacked - ? - Nice, but seller knowingly sent me an opened package with damaged items
text:
Update: Card Hacked - ? - Nice, but seller knowingly sent me an opened package with damaged items. Update: No idea if there is any relationship to this seller, but I note that my debit card I used for this purchase was hacked shortly after leaving my somewhat negative review. Who knows?

I got the rose gold toned set. Overall, they are great. Nicely sized too; the spoons for example are well designed and generously sized to function well, and the fork tines are pretty sharp.

I'm not going to say these are super-well made, evidenced by the fact that one of the salad forks came with quite noticeably bent tines. I know how to fix this and, while normally I'd just return the set, right now I just don't want to bother. Two other items in the set had small scratches as well.

What bothers me is that the seller sent me a ripped-open box which had obviously been returned to them by a prior customer, presumably due to the damaged fork. But the seller went ahead and tried to re-sell it. I guess it did work for them, because I'm not going to bother returning it. However, I'll put it this way: I had been planning to purchase other items from this seller but, now, definitely never will; and of course I'm obligated out of respect to other shoppers to leave an honest review.

Even if the seller stepped up and offered to replace the damaged item, the fact that it chose to send out clearly damaged goods is a sign of a dishonest and unreliable company. What ever happened to doing things right? Seller-customer interactions should be win/win; good for both parties.
